newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian firm ups its 1996 pre-tax revenue 33 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian firm ups its 1996 pre-tax revenue 33 pct.

text.p: Bosnia's Energoinvest engineering company on Wednesday reported pre-tax revenues 230 million German marks ($134 million) in 1996, a rise of 33 percent over 1995.
The Sarajevo-based company, with 90 percent state capital, said it made 46.4 million German Marks in exports, an increase of 40 percent from 33.1 million marks in 1995.
"Most of our export income comes from electric product sales and long-distance power lines," company spokesman Sefik Vucijak told Reuters.
Energoinvest's factories and facilities, scattered throughout Bosnia, suffered significant losses during the devastating 1992-1995 Bosnian war from which the company is struggling to recover.
Vucijak said Energoinvest made $2.27 billion in pre-tax revenue in 1990, the last year it published its results before fighting broke out in 1992.
"The company's 1996 income just shows how the war ate it up. It's a reality, but these figures are good under the circumstances," a foreign economic expert said.

The company invested 8.86 million marks in 1996 to revive some of its factories and called back to work 1,800 employees, marking a 98.8 increase in the number workers compared to 1995 -- but still far from its 45,000 pre-war work force.
The company won a $59 million contract to install 847 kms (525 miles) of long-distance power lines in Libya last year. ($ = 1.716 German Marks)
